spouse: Harriet Reynolds (1803 - 12 Nov 1827); later Laura Collins (b. before 1827)
note: Earliest Taylor yet identified. Harriet died 12 Nov 1827, when her son William was 21 months old.
Died at 8 months. The William born in Feb 1826 was named after him - the ordinary Victorian practice.

*** A RETIRED CAVALRY SERGEANT. *** 1891 census, Northam: 'Cab driver retired sergt p cavaloy' - cab driver, retired sergeant, cavalry. 1901 census: 'Army pensioner', widower, of North Street, Northam. So the Taylors lived by horses too. Father of Mary Septima; died two years after his wife.
source: MyHeritage tree; 1891 and 1901 censuses of Northam (RG13/2163 f.71 p.15 sch.99)

note: 17 years younger than her husband. BRAYLEY is a distinctly Devon surname (from Bray, north Devon) - but the 1891 census records her as BORN IN LONDON, MIDDLESEX, not Devon. Worth resolving.
Children: William Archibald (1893), Gladys Helen (Jun 1900). Same birth month as Kathleen - twins, or one date is wrong.
5th daughter; Irene's twin, female, name unrecorded

*** THE SEVENTH DAUGHTER - which is exactly what "Septima" means. *** Baptised Northam 30 Oct 1884. A PUPIL TEACHER: the 1901 census (31 Mar) calls her "School teacher, 16"; the Exeter Diocesan Board results in the Western Times (4 Apr 1901) place her in Class III of Set II, "monitors over sixteen and pupil teachers in their first year". NOT PRESENT in the 1891 census household, aged 6 - unexplained.
source: MyHeritage tree; Devon Baptisms 1843A/PR/1/16; 1901 census; Western Times 4 Apr 1901 p.7; burial confirmed by Maitland Road Cemetery register, Nov 1935, aged 51
